av_event.what: Right after the short laugh his lopsided grin drops. He looks down and off to the side, away from the screen, for about two seconds with a flat expression, then looks back up at the camera.

text:
B: Alright! Can you hear me? Sorry about the music, there's a nail bar downstairs.
A: Yeah, I can hear it a bit. I'm Gemma.
B: Callum. Where you calling from?
A: Peterborough. You?
B: Catford, South London. Peterborough, that's the Posh, innit? Football.
A: That's us. I go a few times a season with my partner and my brother. Who d'you support?
B: Palace. Mostly from the pub, to be fair. Selhurst tickets aren't cheap.
A: Do you play at all?
B: Used to do five-a-side on Thursdays. Packed it in, though. Fell out with the bloke running it, proper jobsworth, you get me.
A: Ha. I play Wednesdays, mixed league. I'm probably the jobsworth in ours, to be fair. I keep the score.
B: Nah, keeping score's fine. He used to fine you a quid for being late. Who does that?
A: Sounds sensible to me. Were you late a lot?
B: Couple of times. Southeastern, innit, the trains are a joke. Anyway. What d'you do?
A: Quality engineer. Engines and generators. When parts come in wrong, I find out why.
B: Like an investigator.
A: Sort of. Lot of spreadsheets. Lot of asking people for the data until they give it me. What about you?
B: Media and comms at uni, second year. And production work on the side, events. Setting up rigs for warehouse parties, lights, sound, all that.
A: Is that paid, or just helping mates?
B: Paid. Cash, mostly. It's more about the contacts, though. I want to get into music marketing, running campaigns for labels, that kind of thing.
A: Have you applied for anything?
B: Erm, not yet. Everyone keeps asking me that today, honestly. Martin asked, Claire asked.
A: Probably because it's the obvious question, to be fair. I'm not having a go.
B: Nah, I know, I know. It's just, that world's not like engineering. You don't fill in a form. You know someone who knows someone.
A: We've got a placement lad at work, actually, media degree, doing our internal comms. He got it through his uni careers service. Might be worth a look, yeah?
B: Yeah, maybe. Sound. So what d'you do for fun, apart from bossing people about at football?
A: Parkrun on Saturdays, the dog, pub quiz. And one proper holiday a year. I did Iceland for my fortieth.
B: Iceland's sick. I went to a festival in Croatia a couple of years back. Stuck it on a credit card, still paying it off, ha.
A: That's the thing with festivals. I'd have done a spreadsheet first.
B: A spreadsheet? For a holiday?
A: Every year. Budget, flights, what the dog costs in kennels. Dean thinks I'm mad.
B: Nah, that's actually smart, ngl. I want to do Vietnam and Thailand properly. Once the loan comes in.
A: Go in the summer, so you're not missing lectures. And price it up first.
B: Yes, boss. That half-done plaster in your photo, though, that was stressing me out.
A: Ha! That's my spare room. I'm doing it myself. It'll be done when it's done.
B: You plaster? Fair play.
A: Badly, but yeah. It's cheaper than paying someone, and I quite like it.
